title: Ali's death
hook: Ali is struck in the mosque at Kufa during Ramadan, and asks that his killer be treated fairly (reported)

segments.voice: Yesterday: the shield and the qadi. Ali lost his claim in court for lack of a witness. Your line was the caliph lost the case.

It is Ramadan, still dark, and people are coming into the mosque at Kufa for the dawn prayer. Ali, the caliph, is among them. So is a man named Ibn Muljam, and he has a sword. He is one of the Kharijites, the ones who declared Ali an unbeliever for agreeing to talk at Siffin. Umar fell at this same hour, in Medina. Now Ibn Muljam strikes Ali on the head. The wound is deep, and Ali is carried home. What he says in the days that follow is the reason this lesson exists.
screen: `DARK, AND RAMADAN.` → `A SWORD AT DAWN PRAYER.` → `CARRIED HOME.`

segments.voice: Reports say that when he was struck, Ali said: by the Lord of the Ka'bah, I have won. Shia and Sunni sources both carry versions of this: a man struck down at prayer, in the month of fasting, counting it as victory. Then come his instructions about the man who did it. The histories, and the letter of counsel to his sons Hasan and Husayn kept in Nahj al-Balagha, give them like this. Keep him well. Feed him, and give him somewhere decent to stay. If I live, I will decide what to do with him; I may forgive him. If I die, then one blow for one blow. Do not kill anyone else on my account. And do not mutilate him, because the Prophet, peace be upon him, forbade mutilation, even of a rabid dog. Set that against the times: a city in turmoil, a ruler struck by a man who called him an unbeliever, and the dying man's worry is that his own side might go too far. No mob, no revenge on a whole tribe. Only what the law allows, with forgiveness left open. Ali died of the wound soon after. Sunni Muslims honor him as the fourth rightly guided caliph. Shia Muslims mourn him as the first Imam, and observe the nights of his wounding and his death in Ramadan with prayer and grief. His shrine at Najaf, in Iraq, is where Shia Muslims hold he is buried, and pilgrims go there. The fitnah was not over, but this is how Ali left it.
screen: `I HAVE WON, BY THE LORD OF THE KA'BAH.` · `FEED HIM. KEEP HIM WELL.` · `ONE BLOW FOR ONE BLOW, NO MORE.` · `MOURNED IN RAMADAN.` · then, large: `FAIR TO HIS KILLER.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind someone who has truly wronged you, and notice what you'd like to happen to them. Ask Ali's narrower question: what would be fair, and no more? Let go of the extra blow, the story told to everyone; if you pray, you can leave the rest with God.
Ali's death. Struck at the dawn prayer in Kufa, in Ramadan, by a Kharijite, he asked, the reports say, that his killer be kept well and treated within the law, and no further. Today's word.
Your line: fair to his killer. Justice, and not one blow more. That's day eight hundred eighty-six.

howItsDone: Shia Muslims mourn Ali's wounding and death on nights of Ramadan with prayer and gatherings and visit his shrine at Najaf; Sunni Muslims honor him as the fourth rightly guided caliph and retell his instructions about his killer.

chat.meaning: The histories and Nahj al-Balagha give his words: keep him well, one blow for one blow if I die, kill no one else, and do not mutilate him.

notes: Audit: garbled 'Hold that against the times' fixed to 'Set that against the times'. 'Feed him, give him somewhere decent to stay' comes from the histories rather than Nahj al-Balagha letter 47; the teach credits both together, confirm.
The outline marks the instructions as 'reported'; the script attributes them to the histories and Nahj al-Balagha letter 47 (numbering varies by edition). Confirm wording and sources.
'By the Lord of the Ka'bah, I have won' is reported in Shia sources and some Sunni ones; the script says 'Shia and Sunni sources both carry versions of this'. Confirm.

'A few days later' and 'the fourth of the rightly guided caliphs': confirm these are acceptable under the claims rule (the four are a standard Sunni designation already used on day 881). Specific Ramadan dates are omitted on purpose.
Najaf: Shia Muslims hold he is buried there; some Sunni traditions name other places. The script attributes the burial site to Shia belief only.
Ibn Muljam is identified as a Kharijite, which ties back to day 884; confirm.
